questions.q: Which protozoon is a large intestinal amoeba?

options.e: Correct. It lives in the large intestine.

Which of the following is a non-pathogenic amoeba?

options.e: Correct. A harmless commensal that may be confused with E. histolytica.

questions.q: The word histolytica literally means:

options.e: Correct. It causes intestinal and extraintestinal infection.

questions.q: E. histolytica has how many hosts and what type of life cycle?

options.e: Correct. Humans are the definitive host.

questions.q: The infective stage of E. histolytica is the:

questions.q: Which feature describes the E. histolytica trophozoite?

options.t: Two nuclei and four flagella pairs
Central karyosome, fine peripheral chromatin, pseudopodia
options.e: Correct. Cytoplasm has ectoplasm and endoplasm.

questions.q: The E. histolytica cyst contains:

options.t: One to four nuclei and may show cigar-shaped chromatoid bodies
options.e: Correct. Nuclei identical to the trophozoite.

questions.q: Where does excystation of E. histolytica occur?

options.e: Wrong. Cysts pass through the acid.
Correct. After passing stomach acid, trypsin lyses the cyst wall.

questions.q: Where do E. histolytica trophozoites live?

options.t: Mucous and submucous layers of the large intestine

questions.q: Which stool form usually contains E. histolytica cysts?

options.e: Correct. Trophozoites are found in diarrheal stool.

questions.q: Why are trophozoites not infective by mouth?

options.t: They are rapidly destroyed outside the body and cannot survive saliva and gastric acid
options.e: Correct. Cysts are the transmitting stage.

options.t: They are always killed in the colon

questions.q: A hallmark intestinal lesion of amoebiasis is:

options.t: Flask-shaped ulcer in the large intestine
options.e: Correct. Seen in invasive intestinal amoebiasis.

questions.q: The most common extra-intestinal site of amoebiasis is the:

options.e: Correct. Spread is via the portal blood.

questions.q: Which is true about amoebic liver abscess?

options.e: Wrong. It is the drug of choice.

options.t: Stool exam is often negative so serology is helpful
options.e: Correct. The lesion is closed, with no cysts or trophozoites in stool.

questions.q: The drug of choice for amoebic dysentery is:

options.e: Correct. 500-750 mg three times daily for 5-10 days.

questions.q: Which feature identifies Balantidium coli?

options.t: Large kidney-shaped macronucleus and small micronucleus
options.e: Correct. Also has cilia and rapid motility.

questions.q: Why does Balantidium coli never form extraintestinal abscesses?

options.e: Correct. The large size prevents bloodstream spread.

options.t: Because it infects only the stomach

questions.q: Which is true about Giardia lamblia?

options.t: Its infective stage is the trophozoite
It lives in the duodenum and upper jejunum and does not invade tissue
options.e: Correct. It adheres with a ventral sucking disc.

questions.q: Giardia cysts are important in spread because they:

options.t: Are the stage found only in diarrheal stool
options.e: Wrong. Cysts are typical in non-diarrheal stool.

options.t: Are resistant to chlorine and survive months in cold water
options.e: Correct. They are the infective stage.

questions.q: Malabsorption of fat in giardiasis produces:

options.t: Steatorrhea with offensive pale fatty stool and no blood
options.e: Correct. The stool floats in water.

questions.q: The test used when stool is negative but giardiasis is strongly suspected is the:

options.e: Correct. Sampling the upper small intestine.
